Alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection rollout last night we're seeing a ~10m silence window in token-level metrics for several routes. per-token counters for some kernels dropped to zero.
Maria: Do you mean dashboards empty or the exporter shows no emissions? :eyes:
Alex: Dashboards empty, but digging into logs shows exporter warnings. Excerpt: ```2026-03-17T22:14:05Z exporter.go:213 WARN dropped=128 reason=payload_too_large route=payment-checkout kernel_selector=k8-opt```
Ben: 409/413 from the exporter usually means our batching heuristic hit a payload/size limit. Did the kernel selector change add high-cardinality tags?
Alex: Yes — kernel_selector now appends kernel_hash + kernel_variant as tags. Cardinality for redwood.token_latency.per_token jumped ~120k -> ~420k unique tag tuples. Exporter started failing on batch encode.
Jules: @infra-bot can you confirm exporter error spike and open a ticket? We need to ensure we don't lose token-level timing.
infra-bot: metrics-alert: exporter_errors spike 2026-03-17T22:12->22:25. Top reason: payload_too_large. Ticket INF-672 created.
Maria: Can we backfill the missing interval? Are raw samples still in kafka or traces? We should avoid permanent data loss for per-route KPIs.
Ben: We still have raw telemetry in the inference-telemetry Kafka topic for 72h. Plan: run a targeted backfill replayer that re-emits sanitized statsd points. Steps: 1) snapshot offsets 2) run replayer with --strip-tags kernel_hash --map kernel_hash->kernel_category 3) emit to prod-statsd canary then prod.
Alex: Trying a staging canary now: ```./replayer --topic inference-telemetry --offset 451234 --limit 100000 --dest staging-statsd --strip-tags=kernel_hash --map=kernel_hash:kernel_category```
Jules: Dashboard note — make per-route token P95 panels tolerant to absent kernel detail. Add a fallback series grouped by kernel_category and aggregate on route+model to avoid empty charts.
Maria: Mid-term: ops should adjust statsd->otlp emitter to consider tag-cardinality when forming batches (split earlier), and add a disk-backed buffer so transient 409s don't drop telemetry. Also add an alert for sustained payload_too_large errors.
deploy-bot: deploy started: revert 'kernel-tagging' on canary at 1835010200
Ben: After reverting the tagging change on canary, exporter errors dropped back to baseline. Backfill job queued (kvcache-metrics-replayer, job id backfill-18350). I'll create a short postmortem and include kernel selection perf profile that triggered the tagging change.
Alex: For the postmortem include: 1) kernel selector commit hash (a7c9f2) 2) profiling snapshot showing increase in tag emission points 3) timeline of exporter 409s and revert.
Maria: Great. After backfill completes let's run the per-route KPIs (token_p50/p95/p99) against the re-emitted series and compare to pre-rollout baselines. :thumbsup:
Ben: I'll follow up with runbook edits: - don't attach kernel_hash in statsd by default - emit kernel_category instead - add exporter backpressure metric to dashboards.
Jules: Thanks team — status looks good now but we should schedule a deeper audit of metric tag growth before future kernel selector changes. :calendar:
